title: Paul: Abraham justified by faith not works; conclude faith without works of law
source_text: XXVII. Qua in re praeeuntem habemus Apostolum Paulum, qui in suis Epistolis idem frequenter urget & inculcat, praesertim cap. 4. epist. ad Rom. ubi docet Abrahamum non esse justificatum ex operibus, sed ex fide, juxta illud Scripturae, Credidit Abraham Deo, & imputatum est ei ad justitiam. Unde colligit Deum justificare non operantem, sed credentem, & imputare homini justitiam absque operibus, etiam Davidis testimonio confirmat. Capite vero praecedenti, haec est ejus conclusio, multis ante argumentis probata & confirmata, Concludimus hominem fide justificari absque operibus legis. Quibus consentanea sunt quae scribit ad Galatas, cap. 2. v. 16. Scientes, inquit, non justificari hominem ex operibus legis, sed per fidem Jesu Christi, etiam in Christum Jesum credidimus, ut justificaremur ex fide Christi, & non ex operibus legis: propterea quod non justificabitur ex operibus legis ulla caro.
pass_a_gloss: In which matter we have the Apostle Paul going before, who in his letters frequently urges and presses the same—especially Romans 4, where he teaches that Abraham was not justified from works but from faith, according to the Scripture: Abraham believed God, and it was imputed to him for righteousness. From which he gathers that God justifies not the one who works but the one who believes, and imputes righteousness to a person without works—confirmed also by David's testimony. And in the preceding chapter this is his conclusion, proved and confirmed by many arguments before: We conclude that a person is justified by faith without works of the law. To which agree what he writes to the Galatians (2:16): Knowing that a person is not justified from works of the law but through faith in Jesus Christ, even we have believed in Christ Jesus that we might be justified from faith in Christ and not from works of the law; because by works of the law no flesh will be justified.
pass_b_english: Paul's Rom 4: Abraham justified by faith, not works; God justifies the believer.
Conclusion (Rom 3:28; Gal 2:16): justified by faith without works of the law.

lemmas.gloss: not the one who works, but the one who believes

choices.why: Paul's forensic summary of justification by faith.
